findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping when loading documents
findings.body: When document IDs overlap across tenants, `db.find({ documentId })` can return another tenant’s document. The previous implementation included `ctx.tenantId` in the query, so this change introduces a cross-tenant data-disclosure path.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the exported cache module
findings.body: Downstream TypeScript code importing `src/cache` or `readCached` will fail module resolution because the exported module is deleted without a replacement. This breaks the existing exported API despite the stated intent to preserve contracts.

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping when loading documents
findings.body:
For tenants containing the same `documentId`, querying only by `{ documentId }` can return another tenant’s document, causing cross-tenant data disclosure.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the exported cache module
findings.body:
Any existing TypeScript consumer importing `src/cache` or `readCached` now fails compilation/module resolution because the entire exported module was deleted.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping when loading documents
findings.body:
In a shared multi-tenant database, an authenticated user who knows or guesses another tenant’s document ID can retrieve it because `ctx.tenantId` is no longer included in the query. This creates a direct cross-tenant data disclosure vulnerability.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
